title: How to Keep Humidity Down in Your House
h1: How Do You Keep Humidity Down in Your House?
description: Foggy windows, musty smells and damp closets mean your home holds too much moisture. Learn practical ways to lower indoor humidity and keep it under control.
quick_answer: Vent moisture out at the source with bathroom and kitchen fans, run your air conditioner, and use a dehumidifier where the house stays damp. Fix leaks, keep gutters and sprinklers away from the walls, and seal leaky ducts. Aim to keep indoor humidity between about 30 and 50 percent.
body:
Near the coast, humidity is one of the most common comfort complaints we hear about. Marine air rolls in, the house feels clammy, closets start to smell, and windows fog up on cool mornings. Inland homes can have the same problem after a rainy stretch or when moisture from daily life has nowhere to go.

How do you know your house is too humid?

  • Condensation on windows, especially in the morning
  • Musty smells in closets, bathrooms or the whole house
  • Mold or mildew on bathroom ceilings, window frames or behind furniture
  • A sticky, clammy feeling even when the temperature is fine
  • Peeling paint or warped wood trim
  • Allergy symptoms that get worse at home

A digital hygrometer gives you the real number. Over about 50 to 60 percent for long stretches, mold and dust mites start to thrive.

What are the simplest ways to lower humidity?

Daily living adds a lot of moisture to the air. Showers, cooking, laundry, even breathing. Getting that moisture out is the first step:

  1. Run bathroom fans during every shower and for 15 to 20 minutes after. Make sure the fan actually vents outside, not into the attic.
  2. Use the range hood when you cook, especially when boiling water.
  3. Check the dryer vent. A disconnected or clogged vent dumps warm, wet air into the house or attic.
  4. Don't dry laundry indoors on damp days.
  5. Keep closet doors cracked and leave space between furniture and exterior walls so air can move.
  6. Cut back on houseplants or overwatering if a room stays damp.

Does running the air conditioner lower humidity?

Yes. An air conditioner removes moisture as it cools, which is why there's a condensate drain. But it only works if the system runs long enough. An oversized system cools the house quickly and shuts off before it pulls much moisture out, leaving you cool but clammy.

Other things that make an AC worse at removing moisture include a dirty coil, a clogged filter, the fan set to "On" instead of "Auto," and low airflow. A tune-up takes care of most of these. Some newer systems have variable-speed blowers and dehumidification settings that run longer at lower speed to pull out more moisture.

When do you need a dehumidifier?

If the house stays damp after you've vented moisture and the AC is working well, a dehumidifier is the next step.

  • Portable dehumidifiers work for a single problem room, like a bedroom, garage or laundry room. Empty or drain the tank and clean the filter regularly.
  • Whole-home dehumidifiers connect to your ductwork and control humidity throughout the house, with no tanks to empty. They're a good fit for coastal homes that stay damp most of the year, including mild months when the AC doesn't run.

Our indoor air quality team can measure humidity in your home and recommend the right size and type.

What hidden problems cause high humidity?

Sometimes moisture is coming from somewhere you can't see:

  • Leaky return ducts in a crawl space or attic pulling in damp air
  • A damp crawl space with bare soil and no vapor barrier
  • Plumbing leaks inside walls or under sinks
  • Sprinklers soaking the stucco and foundation
  • Gutters dumping water next to the house
  • A clogged condensate drain letting water back up near the air handler

If you've tried the basics and the house still feels damp, it's worth having someone look for these sources. Fixing the source is better than running a dehumidifier around the clock.

Does humidity affect your energy use?

It does. Damp air feels warmer than dry air at the same temperature, so many people turn the thermostat down to feel comfortable. Bringing humidity down often lets you set the thermostat a degree or two higher and feel just as cool. Moisture control and comfort go hand in hand.

Can humidity get too low?

It can. Below about 30 percent you'll notice dry skin, static and scratchy throats, which happens inland during Santa Ana winds. The goal is a steady middle range, not as dry as possible.
faqs: What is a good indoor humidity level?
Between about 30 and 50 percent is comfortable for most people and helps limit mold and dust mites. Coastal homes often run higher and may need help staying in that range.
Why is my house so humid even with the AC on?
An oversized system, a dirty coil, low airflow or the fan set to run constantly can all keep the AC from removing moisture. A technician can check the system and settings.
Only when the air outside is drier than the air inside. Near the coast on foggy or marine-layer days, opening windows can actually bring more moisture in.
For homes that stay damp most of the year, often near the coast, a whole-home unit keeps humidity steady without emptying tanks or running portable units in every room.
